page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon processor running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs, which correspond to 8 physical cores and 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU features a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, with support for AVX, AVX512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of this instance consistently in the average range. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng yield scores of 1824.08 and 15445.03, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate a read-only cached small block speed of 840.5 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds reach 82.77 GB/sec and 56.23 GB/sec. In application-specific benchmarks, the instance achieves 15.3 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 16.5 GB/sec. For language model workloads, prompt processing with a small 135M model reaches 1252.41 tokens per second, though performance drops to a weak 31.18 tokens per second when processing prompts for a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.u1-c1m4.4xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for standard enterprise workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider. This instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight text or image processing tasks.

It does not include local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results indicate steady, average-tier performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8674.0 and a Redis SET throughput of 15.3 million operations per second. The instance is qualitatively cost-effective for standard workloads that do not require high-speed local NVMe or specialized accelerators.
